prompt: Prime-time adult animated sitcom characters, simple rounded people with big round eyes, small dot pupils and overbites, flat colour and black outlines everywhere except the faces, which are rendered with startling real skin: pores, stubble, sweat, tired wet eyes. Every flat colour is laid on with thick visible oil brushstrokes. Only the bodies, clothes and places are cartoon: every face in the frame, however small, is painted as real human skin with wrinkles, pores, bags under the eyes and real eyelids, far more lifelike than anything around it, and no feature is exaggerated. Low in a packed crowd in a 1930s city square: large in the foreground, a heavy-set clean-shaven Black baker in his fifties with a shaved head, a broken nose and a round double chin, in a floury vest under an old coat, looks up with one hand stretched open, hopeful, as a stream of blank white envelopes sails right over his fingers on the wind and away. Around him others reach up too, young and old, men and women, white and South Asian. Behind, up on a stone balcony, a tall skinny mayor in a bowler hat with a gold chain beams and waves. Grey morning sky. Plain margins with no writing. Thanks.
